nodes.label: Superpowers Project
nodes.rationale: The overall subject of RELEASE-NOTES.md: an open-source collection of skills for AI coding agents (obra/superpowers). Treated as a named project concept because the release notes track its releases, skills, and harness integrations.

nodes.label: Subagent-Driven Development (SDD) Skill
nodes.rationale: Named skill repeatedly featured across releases (review redesign, plan-scoped workspaces, native vs subagent execution). A core named skill of the project, so extracted as a concept.

nodes.label: Brainstorming Skill
nodes.rationale: Named core skill (design/requirements phase, visual companion, hard gates). Extracted as a named concept; it is the entry point of the skill pipeline.

nodes.label: Writing Plans Skill
nodes.rationale: Named core skill that produces implementation plans (Review Focus section, self-review loops). Part of the brainstorm -> plan -> execute pipeline.

nodes.label: Executing Plans Skill

nodes.label: Using Superpowers Bootstrap Skill
nodes.rationale: Named bootstrap skill injected into every session (size trimmed in v6.1.0, rationalization tables, SUBAGENT-STOP gate). It is the project's entry/bootstrap mechanism.

nodes.label: Test-Driven Development (TDD) Skill
nodes.rationale: Named core skill (green = project suite, testing-anti-patterns reference, 'Why Order Matters' rationalization rows). Extracted as a named concept.

nodes.label: Systematic Debugging Skill
nodes.rationale: Named core skill (bundles root-cause-tracing, defense-in-depth, condition-based-waiting, find-polluter.sh). Extracted as a named concept.

It is the project's small logo (assets/superpowers-small.svg).

nodes.label: Design goal: diagnose superpowers sessions with path:line evidence
nodes.rationale: Ship skills/diagnosing-superpowers, a pure-prose skill that helps a human partner pin down what went wrong in a session, reports what happened with path:line evidence, exports a scrubbed bundle, files a GitHub issue, and searches for similar local sessions.

nodes.label: Architecture: one lean SKILL.md plus prompts/, references/, templates/ with no shipped scripts
nodes.rationale: One lean SKILL.md (workflow, hard rules, Red Flags) plus one file per subagent job under prompts/, per-harness session-store references under references/, and output recipes under templates/. No shipped scripts because the model does the work using jq/python3/shell it already has.

nodes.label: Development process: RED baseline scenarios, GREEN with skill, REFACTOR loopholes
nodes.rationale: Skill content is developed RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR per superpowers:writing-skills: baseline scenarios first, skill written to the observed failures, re-run, loopholes closed, so the Red Flags table and hard rules are grounded in observed agent rationalizations rather than design hypotheses.

nodes.label: Constraint: field-level claims only for verified harness formats
nodes.rationale: No invented harness formats: field-level claims appear only in references/claude-code-sessions.md (verified against Claude Code 2.1.247 transcripts) and references/codex-sessions.md (verified against Codex CLI 0.147.0 / 0.149.0 rollouts); every other harness goes through the discovery procedure so the report reader can judge inferred layouts.

nodes.label: Constraint: skill prose says 'your human partner', never 'the user'
nodes.rationale: The skill addresses a collaborator, not a customer: keeping 'your human partner' frames the agent as working alongside the person, consistent with superpowers conventions; the structure test enforces it by grepping for 'the user'.

nodes.label: Constraint: SKILL.md description 'Use when' third person, body under 1000 words
nodes.rationale: A trigger-style description without workflow summary keeps SKILL.md a router, not a runbook; the 1000-word body budget is enforced by the structure test so the skill stays lean and quick to load.

nodes.label: Constraint: no machine-specific paths or person names in shipped files
nodes.rationale: Shipped files must be portable: no /Users/ or /home/ paths and no person's name (session UUIDs are fine), so the skill works on any executor's machine; the structure test scans for leaks.

nodes.label: Constraint: session files are never modified, moved, or deleted
nodes.rationale: The transcript is the evidence base: any modification destroys the audit trail that path:line citations point at, so diagnosis must be strictly read-only.

nodes.label: Constraint: human approval before archiving or posting
nodes.rationale: Nothing is archived before the human partner has seen the scrub log and file list, and nothing is posted to GitHub before approval of the exact text, because unapproved export can leak private data and an unapproved issue publicly commits the team to a claim.

nodes.label: Constraint: the skill never names a defect or proposes a change to superpowers
nodes.rationale: The agent reports evidence; whether superpowers needs a change is the triager's call. The single allowed statement is the report's 'Superpowers involvement: not indicated / possible / likely' line with its evidence, which keeps the bundle a neutral evidence pack instead of a self-justifying bug report.

nodes.label: Core principle: every finding cites path:line, no citation no finding
nodes.rationale: Findings without a path:line citation are dropped by the dispatcher, which forces evidence-backed reporting and lets the human partner or a maintainer re-verify every claim against the original files.

nodes.label: Mechanism: context-safety reading of transcripts (counts and line numbers first, then trimmed fields)
nodes.rationale: A single transcript line can be a megabyte, so never cat or grep a transcript for content: check wc -lc and long lines first, get line numbers and counts, then extract small fields from specific lines, to keep the agent's own context from blowing up.

nodes.label: Workspace: ~/.superpowers/diagnosing-superpowers/<session-id>/
nodes.rationale: Per-session workspace directory where the case file, report, and bundle live; the skill prints the path when it creates it and again in the report so the human partner always knows where artifacts are.

nodes.label: Local fixtures: CC-huge, CC-compact, CC-this, CX-big, CX-sub transcripts
nodes.rationale: Five real local transcripts chosen by characteristics (size, max line length, compaction present, subagents present, live session) serve as test fixtures for scenarios; executors on other machines pick equivalents and record the substitution, and fixture paths never ship.

nodes.label: Proposed file structure of skills/diagnosing-superpowers
nodes.rationale: SKILL.md plus CREATION-LOG.md, references/ (claude-code-sessions, codex-sessions, other-harnesses), prompts/ (seven analyst dimensions plus scrub, scrub-audit, similar-session), templates/ (case, report, bundle-README, issue), a bash structure test, and a one-line README entry.

nodes.label: Task 1: eleven RED baseline scenarios dispatched to fresh subagents without the skill
nodes.rationale: Eleven complaint-shaped scenarios (vague/hurried, authority push, huge line, export in a hurry, subagent misdirection, retrieval, too long, extra work, expensive, live session, issue handoff) establish the failure baseline; observed rationalizations are collected verbatim to drive the Red Flags table.

nodes.label: tests/diagnosing-superpowers/test-skill-structure.sh: shell structure test
nodes.rationale: Checks what a shell can check: frontmatter name/description shape, SKILL.md word budget, required sections, referenced files exist, no local paths or names leaked, no 'the user' in prose; behavior is tested by scenarios, so the test stays RED until SKILL.md lands (Task 6).

nodes.label: references/claude-code-sessions.md: Claude Code session store field map and safe extraction
nodes.rationale: Verified against Claude Code 2.1.247: main/subagent transcript locations under ~/.claude/projects, line-type envelope, field map for prompts, tool calls, skill invocation and attribution, tokens, hooks, compaction, plus jq/python3 size-safe extraction recipes.

nodes.label: references/codex-sessions.md: Codex rollout field map and safe extraction
nodes.rationale: Verified against Codex CLI 0.147.0/0.149.0: rollout file layout under ~/.codex/sessions, session_meta/turn_context/response_item/event_msg line types, field map for identity, prompts, tool calls, turn timing, cumulative tokens, compaction, subagent linkage, and jq recipes that never print a whole line.

nodes.label: references/other-harnesses.md: six-step discovery procedure for unverified harnesses
nodes.rationale: For any harness without a verified reference: ask the harness, look under its config directory, confirm a candidate by its first human message, map needed fields, record store path and confidence in coverage notes, and if the store cannot be found ask the human partner instead of guessing another harness's layout.

nodes.label: templates/case.md: case file the controller fills before dispatching analysts
nodes.rationale: Captures the agreed problem statement, session inventory (id, path, lines, bytes, longest line, first prompt), rejected candidates, environment (OS, harness, models, superpowers install root/version/sha, sha1 of skill files read or injected, other plugins), and the context-safety rules every analyst must follow.

nodes.label: templates/report.md: diagnosis report with REQUIRED slots
nodes.rationale: Nine sections, every REQUIRED slot filled or replaced with 'none found - checked: <what>': problem statement, triage verdict with confidence, environment, sessions examined, per-turn timeline, findings for seven dimensions, superpowers involvement (not indicated / possible / likely only), coverage notes, and optional similar-sessions table.

nodes.label: templates/bundle-README.md: README for the export bundle with redaction levels
nodes.rationale: Explains what a scrubbed bundle is (an evidence pack, by design containing no diagnosis of superpowers), lists its files (report, case, environment.json, timeline, findings, condensed transcripts, scrub-log), how to read it via [L<n>] line markers, and the three redaction levels: skeleton, evidence, full.

nodes.label: templates/issue.md: GitHub issue body conforming to the repo bug_report template
nodes.rationale: Follows .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md so created issues satisfy it: environment table, superpowers-vs-platform question, problem statement plus triage verdict with path:line rewritten as transcript line numbers, and an explicit 'this report does not propose a fix' stance.

nodes.label: Common analyst subagent header block (read CASE first, context safety, finding return format)
nodes.rationale: Every analyst prompt starts with the same verbatim header: read the case file first, follow its context-safety rules, 'the current session' is not a thing (only paths in CASE count), and return only findings in the report-section shape with path:line evidence plus a Checked line, so a finding without a citation gets discarded by the dispatcher.

nodes.label: prompts/skill-timeline.md: analyst dimension - skill and plugin timeline, missed/late triggers
nodes.rationale: Builds the per-human-turn record of skill and plugin use: every skill invocation, every non-superpowers plugin/skill/MCP server/hook, and turns whose request matches a skill's trigger description with no invocation (missed) or an invocation only later (late); it reports the match and the absence and leaves the judgment to the reader.

nodes.label: prompts/plan-adherence.md: analyst dimension - recovered plan vs. what happened
nodes.rationale: Recovers the session's commitments (agreed plans, spec files, todo lists), marks structural events between commitment and execution (compaction, resumes, aborts, subagent dispatches), and reports skipped, out-of-order, silently changed, invented, or post-structural-event-drift steps.

nodes.label: prompts/repeated-work.md: analyst dimension - duplicated reads/edits/commands/dispatches
nodes.rationale: Extracts every tool call as (line, turn, tool, key), groups by (tool, key) with count thresholds (>=3 reads/searches, >=2 edits, non-idempotent shell commands, same subagent description twice), distinguishes re-reads after an edit (not a finding) from re-reads after a compaction or with nothing in between, and flags re-derived decisions.

nodes.label: prompts/stumbles.md: analyst dimension - errors, retries, reverts, corrections
nodes.rationale: Finds every point where the session stopped going forward: tool errors, failed shell commands, same-turn retries, reverted edits, assistant backtracking phrases, human corrections, permission denials, hook failures, API errors, rate limits, aborted turns, and mid-task compaction, each with recovery status.

nodes.label: prompts/quality-evidence.md: analyst dimension - tests, claim verification, commits, review handling
nodes.rationale: Judges the process against its own claims without reviewing the code: test runs and what followed failures, 'done/fixed/passing' claims with no supporting tool result in the same turn, commit messages that overstate or omit the preceding work, review points acknowledged but not acted on, and acceptance criteria met/not met/not checked.

nodes.label: prompts/request-conflicts.md: analyst dimension - contradictory human instructions
nodes.rationale: Only human-typed prompts count (not hook output, system reminders, tool results, or a parent agent): reports instructions that cannot both be followed, instructions conflicting with a loaded instruction file, instructions to skip or override a step/skill/rule, and scope-changing clarification answers, without judging who was right.

nodes.label: prompts/cost-and-time.md: analyst dimension - token and wall-clock accounting
nodes.rationale: Accounts for where tokens and wall-clock went: per-human-turn and per-subagent token totals (Codex cumulative events differenced), top-5 largest turns, >10-minute gaps, the ten longest tool-result lines, compaction counts and pre/post tokens, and subagent token/duration breakdowns; findings are concentrations with numbers, no speculation.

nodes.label: prompts/scrub.md: scrubber rewrites the bundle in place and writes scrub-log.md
nodes.rationale: Replaces emails, people, org identifiers, secrets, hosts, home paths, repositories (unless public), and proprietary terms with stable numbered placeholders (<EMAIL-n> etc.) applied consistently across every file in the bundle, writes a scrub-log of placeholder -> category -> count without ever writing the original value, and keeps session ids, tool names, skill names, model ids, and line numbers because the bundle is useless without them.

nodes.label: prompts/scrub-audit.md: independent scrub checker returning CLEAN or MISSED
nodes.rationale: A second agent reads every condensed bundle file in full and reports only what the scrubber missed (file:line - category - first 20 characters), never fixing anything and never commenting on quality, so the human partner gets an independent check before archiving.

nodes.label: prompts/similar-session.md: per-candidate signature matcher for similar local sessions
nodes.rationale: Given a diagnosed session's case file, one candidate transcript, and a signature of markers (skill-sequence, error-string, repeated-command, repeated-file, compaction-then, missed-trigger, free), returns match yes/partial/no with per-marker hit/miss/unknown and path:line evidence, enabling the report's similar-sessions section.

nodes.label: Red Flags table in SKILL.md: observed rationalizations vs. reality
nodes.rationale: Rows are design hypotheses that Task 6 edits against CREATION-LOG.md 'Rationalizations observed': keep a row only if a baseline run produced that rationalization (reworded to the verbatim phrase), add rows for uncovered observed rationalizations, and drop rows nothing supports, so the table counters exactly the excuses agents actually make.

nodes.label: Hard rules in SKILL.md: context safety, read-only, exact paths, human prompts only, no diagnosis, approval gates
nodes.rationale: The contract lines of the skill: check sizes before reading and never cat/grep for content, never modify session files, pass absolute paths to subagents, count only human-typed prompts, state superpowers involvement without diagnosing it, and gate archiving and posting on human approval of what they saw.

nodes.label: SKILL.md workflow: intake, locate, triage with seven analysts, report, GitHub issues, export, similar sessions
nodes.rationale: Seven-step workflow with conditional steps 5-7: problem intake one question at a time until a real problem statement exists, locate sessions via the harness references and fill the case file, triage by dispatching one analyst per dimension in parallel (splitting long transcripts by turn range) and discarding uncited findings, then fill the report; GitHub search/draft only on approval, export only with a chosen redaction level and CLEAN audit, similar sessions only when asked.

nodes.label: Quick reference table in SKILL.md: complaint to starting dimension
nodes.rationale: Maps common complaints ('it took too long', 'extra work', 'so expensive', 'what is it doing', 'ignored the plan', 'skill X never fired') to the analyst dimensions to start with, so triage begins on the right track.

nodes.label: Micro-tests: five reps per prohibition, control arm vs. skill arm
nodes.rationale: For each prohibition with an observed baseline violation, run 5 fresh subagents with and without the full SKILL.md content and tabulate control vs. skill violations /5 plus variance; a prohibition with 0/5 control violations stays a contract line without Red Flags rows, keeping the table evidence-driven.

nodes.label: GREEN re-run of scenarios 1-11 with per-scenario pass criteria
nodes.rationale: The same eleven scenarios are re-run with 'Read SKILL.md first and follow it' prepended, each with concrete pass criteria (asks instead of analyzing, no superpowers fix, no >2000-char transcript content, no archive before scrub log, absolute paths in subagent prompts, exact issue text shown), with responses recorded verbatim and compared to baseline.

nodes.label: Task 7: end-to-end run on fixture CC-compact recorded in CREATION-LOG.md
nodes.rationale: One full run (intake on 'the session repeated work after a compaction', locate, seven analysts, report, evidence-level export with scrub and audit, GitHub search only) verified against a checklist: workspace path printed, all REQUIRED report sections filled, sha1 table present, absolute paths for every transcript, per-turn token totals, bundle CLEAN with no /Users/ leaks, and no fixture file changed.

nodes.label: Redaction placeholder scheme: <EMAIL-n>, <PERSON-n>, <ORG-n>, <SECRET-n>, <HOST-n>, <REPO-n>, <PROPRIETARY-n>
nodes.rationale: Stable numbered placeholders, one per original value, ordered by first appearance within the bundle, so a reader can correlate redacted values across files while never seeing the originals; home paths are rewritten to ~/ and the account-name segment removed.

nodes.label: Commit convention: messages end with the Claude-Session trailer for this branch
nodes.rationale: Every commit in the plan carries 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DyaGKhTXvHNs2JgPhDktz7' so the branch's work stays traceable back to the session that produced it.

nodes.label: Make SDD review-fix loop convergent and autonomous
nodes.rationale: The current fix loop dispatched dedicated fix subagents and had no round cap, so loops could churn without converging and controllers lost their place across compaction (re-dispatching entire completed task sequences). The redesign must make the loop converge (cap + adjudication) and be autonomous (resume-based rounds, scoped re-reviews).

nodes.label: SKILL.md lifecycle restructure (Setup, Task Loop, Final Review, Common Rationalizations)
nodes.rationale: Reorganizing the skill by lifecycle places the loop rules where the controller reads them per phase; the old Never-list items are distributed into sections and excuse-shaped items become a rationalization table.

nodes.label: Resume-the-implementer fix rounds (rounds 1-3)
nodes.rationale: The original implementer's context is intact (it knows the task, the code, and its own choices), so resuming it with the open findings verbatim avoids the context rebuild and fresh-eyes-only cost of a dedicated fix subagent; the report file is the persistent memory if the harness cannot message a live agent.

nodes.label: Fix-loop escalation: rounds 4-5 dispatch a fresh implementer on a more capable model
nodes.rationale: A loop that survives three resumes usually means the implementer cannot see its own problem; a fresh implementer on a model at least one tier above the one that got stuck combines fresh eyes with a capability bump in one move.

nodes.label: Five-round breaker with controller adjudication at the cap
nodes.rationale: Past the cap, rounds don't converge — the failure is structural. The controller (which holds the plan and cross-task context the reviewer lacks) adjudicates each open finding only at the cap: park contestable/non-load-bearing findings with a ruling, STOP with BLOCKED on load-bearing ones. Adjudicating earlier is pre-judging with a different name; a silent discard is forbidden.

nodes.label: Scoped re-review (verify findings, inspect fix diff only)
nodes.rationale: A full re-review would wander and extend the loop indefinitely; scoping the re-reviewer to the findings list and the fix diff lets it verdict each finding ADDRESSED/NOT ADDRESSED and flag only new breakage the fix introduced, so every round ends with verification without unbounded re-review. Out-of-scope observations go to the ledger as deferred minors, never into the loop.

nodes.label: re-review-prompt.md — new scoped re-review prompt template
nodes.rationale: Proposed new template (Task 1) carrying the scoped re-review contract; adds [FINDINGS] and [FIX_BASE_SHA] placeholders to the existing bracket convention, and instructs the re-reviewer to read the diff file once, stay read-only, and emit per-finding verdicts, new breakage, out-of-scope observations, and a round verdict.

nodes.label: Progress ledger with exact line formats (resume rule)
nodes.rationale: Conversation memory does not survive compaction and controllers that lost their place have re-dispatched entire completed task sequences — the single most expensive failure observed. The ledger (.superpowers/sdd/progress.md) with strict line formats is the recovery map: a task is DONE iff it has a `Task <N>: complete` line, so after compaction the controller trusts the ledger and git log over its own recollection.

nodes.label: Load-bearing vs non-load-bearing finding adjudication (BLOCKED vs parked)
nodes.rationale: Parking a structural failure lets every dependent task build on it and hands the final review a problem it cannot fix either, so load-bearing findings (a later task builds on it, or it reveals a plan defect) must STOP the run with `Task <N>: BLOCKED` and a report to the human, while non-load-bearing findings are parked with an explicit ruling the final review can triage.

nodes.label: Verbatim-move rule (eval-tuned sentences move unchanged)
nodes.rationale: Eval-tuned sentences in SKILL.md were chosen because evals pass with them, so paraphrasing during the restructure risks silent behavior regression; only fix-policy language may be reworded, and every rewording must appear in Task 3's move map so drift is checkable.

nodes.label: Common Rationalizations table in SKILL.md
nodes.rationale: Excuse-shaped items from the old Never list are converted into an Excuse/Reality table so the controller can self-audit its most likely failure modes (e.g., fixing findings itself, skipping the re-review, dropping a finding silently) at the point of use.

nodes.label: scaffoldSddMidloopParked / scaffoldSddMidloopStructural eval fixture helpers
nodes.rationale: The breaker needs a repo mid-SDD-execution: Tasks 1-2 committed, Task 2 at fix round 5/5 with one open finding, Task 3 unstarted, and ledger SHAs that are real fixture commits so a resuming controller can trust ledger + git log. The variant axis is Task 3's call contract: seconds (quality-only finding, breaker should park) vs milliseconds (plan contradiction Task 3 builds on, breaker should BLOCK).

nodes.label: Eval scenario: sdd-fix-loop-resumes-implementer
nodes.rationale: Verifies the core fix mechanism: when a task review finds issues, the controller re-engages the original implementer (SendMessage carrying the findings) instead of dispatching a new fix subagent or editing the code itself; the deterministic core is the tool-called SendMessage transcript check (claude-only, since resume semantics are Claude-specific).

nodes.label: Eval scenario: sdd-breaker-adjudicates-at-cap
nodes.rationale: Verifies the breaker on a non-load-bearing quality finding: after resume at fix round 5/5, the agent must not dispatch a sixth round, must adjudicate the finding itself and record `Task 2: parked — … — ruling: …` plus a parked-completion line, then implement Task 3 through the normal loop.

nodes.label: Eval scenario: sdd-breaker-structural-blocks
nodes.rationale: Verifies the breaker on a load-bearing plan contradiction (Task 3 passes milliseconds into a seconds contract): the pass behavior is the agent STOPPING and surfacing the contradiction to the human instead of parking the finding and implementing Task 3 on top of it; the deterministic checks pin the negatives (no src/summary.js, no Task 3 complete, no fix round 6).

nodes.label: Live RED/GREEN/regression eval campaign (quorum)
nodes.rationale: Before/after evidence is required for the PR: RED baselines run the three new scenarios against dev (expected failures prove the scenarios detect the old behavior), GREEN runs them against the redesign (all must pass), and regression runs the four existing SDD scenarios so the new loop doesn't break established fix cycles; verdicts are recorded in an experiment log with negative results at equal billing.

nodes.label: subagent-driven-development
nodes.rationale: Dispatches a fresh subagent per task with a review after each (most thorough option) so the agent can work autonomously for hours without deviating from the plan.

nodes.label: test-driven-development (RED-GREEN-REFACTOR)
nodes.rationale: Enforces true red/green TDD: write a failing test, watch it fail, write minimal code, watch it pass, commit; code written before tests is deleted to keep tests honest.

nodes.label: brainstorming skill (Socratic design refinement)
nodes.rationale: Activates before writing code and refines rough ideas through questions, exploring alternatives and presenting the design in digestible sections for validation, saving a design document.

nodes.label: writing-plans skill
nodes.rationale: Breaks work into bite-sized 2-5 minute tasks with exact file paths, complete code and verification steps so the plan is followable by an enthusiastic junior engineer with no project context.

nodes.label: executing-plans skill
nodes.rationale: Inline plan execution alternative: one context, one final review of the whole branch at the end; the cheapest execution mode versus per-task subagents.

nodes.label: using-git-worktrees skill
nodes.rationale: Creates an isolated workspace on a new branch after design approval and verifies a clean test baseline so implementation does not disturb the main checkout.

nodes.label: requesting-code-review skill
nodes.rationale: Reviews work against the plan between tasks and reports issues by severity, with critical issues blocking progress.

nodes.label: finishing-a-development-branch skill
nodes.rationale: Verifies tests when tasks complete, then presents merge/PR/keep/discard options and cleans up the worktree.

nodes.label: diagnosing-superpowers skill
nodes.rationale: Reads the session transcript and reports what happened with line-level evidence when a session misbehaves, and can package a scrubbed bundle for a bug report.

nodes.label: using-superpowers bootstrap skill
nodes.rationale: Injects the bootstrap that makes the skills system active at session start; without it (e.g. Hermes sessions compacted past the first turn, or missing hooks) skills stop triggering.

nodes.label: Kimi Code plugin manifest (.kimi-plugin/plugin.json)
nodes.rationale: The manifest points Kimi Code at the existing skills/ directory, loads using-superpowers at session start via sessionStart.skill, and provides Kimi-specific tool mapping via skillInstructions; skills are read in place with no copies, symlinks, hooks or extra runtime dependencies.

nodes.label: Kimi Code tool mapping (AskUserQuestion, TodoList, Agent, Skill, Read/Write/Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob, FetchURL, WebSearch)
nodes.rationale: Skills describe actions instead of hard-coding one runtime's tool names, so on Kimi Code the abstract actions resolve to Kimi's native tool names.

nodes.label: OpenCode bootstrap injection (controller session, compaction handling)
nodes.rationale: Controller sessions receive the using-superpowers bootstrap in transient model context; delegated child sessions keep native skills but not the controller bootstrap; when V2 compaction removes all user messages the plugin appends a transient bootstrap after the checkpoint so skills keep triggering in long sessions.

nodes.label: OpenCode V1/V2 tool mapping (task->subagent, apply_patch->patch, bash->shell, todo dropped in V2)
nodes.rationale: Skills speak in actions rather than naming any one runtime's tools, so the bootstrap maps them to the tools each OpenCode flavor actually exposes; V2 renamed task to subagent, apply_patch to patch, bash to shell, and dropped the todo tool entirely.

nodes.label: Skill Shadowing (personal overrides superpowers)
nodes.rationale: Personal skills override same-named superpowers skills so users can customize behavior without forking the superpowers repo; resolveSkillPath tries personalDir first unless the name is explicitly prefixed superpowers:.

nodes.label: Porting Superpowers to a New Harness
Hard Requirement: Automatic Session-Start Injection
nodes.rationale: The single non-negotiable capability: the harness must inject the bootstrap into the model's context at the start of every session with no per-session opt-in by the human partner; if the only path is opt-in, the port is not a real port.

nodes.label: Harness Capability Checklist
nodes.rationale: Part 2 table of capabilities a harness needs to support Superpowers: skill discovery+invocation, file read/write/edit, shell commands, subagent dispatch, todo tracking, web fetch/search, and polyglot Windows script execution; each marked essential or degradable with a fallback.

nodes.label: Definition of Done for a Port
nodes.rationale: Part 3: a port is finished only when the bootstrap loads every session with no opt-in, a tool mapping exists, skills are invocable, the acceptance test passes, tests cover the integration, and a real user can install it through the harness's own mechanism with the version tracked.

nodes.label: Acceptance Test: brainstorming auto-triggers
nodes.rationale: In a clean session the user message "Let's make a react todo list" must auto-trigger the brainstorming skill before any code is written; the full transcript is required for the PR.

nodes.label: Integration Shape A: Shell-Hook
nodes.rationale: Harness runs a shell command at session start and reads JSON from stdout; the script reads using-superpowers/SKILL.md and prints a harness-specific JSON shape (field name and nesting differ per harness); references: hooks/session-start, hooks/run-hook.cmd, hooks/hooks.json, hooks-cursor.json.

nodes.label: Integration Shape B: In-Process Plugin/Extension
nodes.rationale: Harness loads a JS/TS module with lifecycle callbacks; bootstrap is assembled in code (strip frontmatter, wrap in EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT, inline tool mapping) and injected as a user-role message with a dedup guard and compaction re-injection; references: .opencode/plugins/superpowers.js, .pi/extensions/superpowers.ts.

nodes.label: Integration Shape C: Instructions-File
nodes.rationale: No shell hook or code plugin; the installed extension ships a manifest-declared context file (e.g. Gemini contextFileName -> GEMINI.md) that @-includes the bootstrap skill and tool-mapping reference; the harness loads it raw with no injector.

nodes.label: Porting Procedure (Steps 1-7)
nodes.rationale: Part 5 prescriptive procedure that branches on integration shape: study reference, create manifest/entry point, wire bootstrap injection, write tool mapping, handle no-native-skill-tool, add tests, and install locally then drive a live instance via tmux.

nodes.label: Distribution and Release Channels
nodes.rationale: Part 6: per-harness distribution (marketplace, fork sync, git-URL install, package-manifest fields, local installer), plus rules that the bootstrap must be a file the installer recognizes, exec bits may be stripped so scripts are invoked via interpreter, install docs must be written, and new manifests registered in .version-bump.json.

nodes.label: Rule 1: Skills Name Actions, Not Tools
nodes.rationale: Do not edit skill bodies to fit a harness; a port only adds a tool-mapping reference and a bootstrap injector and never reaches into skills/*/SKILL.md to swap tool names, because skill content is behavior-shaping code.

nodes.label: Rule 2: Ship Through the Harness's Own Install Mechanism
nodes.rationale: The bootstrap, skills, and tool mapping are delivered as part of what the harness installs (plugin/extension/marketplace entry); a port must never hand-edit the user's global or personal config files to inject anything.

nodes.label: Windows / Polyglot Hook (run-hook.cmd)
nodes.rationale: Part 7: hooks/run-hook.cmd is a polyglot valid as both Windows batch and Unix shell; enforces that hook scripts are extensionless (a .sh would be double-invoked by Claude Code's Windows handling) and that there is one extensionless bash script plus the wrapper for all three platforms.

nodes.label: Spec Review Loop (brainstorming skill)
nodes.rationale: Added to the brainstorming skill after the spec is written; dispatch a reviewer, fix issues and re-dispatch until approved. Same agent that wrote the spec fixes it to preserve context, loop is capped at 5 iterations then escalated to a human, and reviewers are advisory so disagreements can be explained.

nodes.label: Plan Review Loop (writing-plans skill)
nodes.rationale: Chunk-by-chunk review added to the writing-plans skill before execution handoff; each chunk is dispatched to a plan reviewer to catch TODOs, scope creep, weak task decomposition, and missing verification steps. Chunks are delimited by '## Chunk N' headings, kept under 1000 lines, and logically self-contained.

nodes.label: Spec Document Reviewer Prompt Template
nodes.rationale: Standardizes the spec reviewer's checks into categories (completeness, coverage, consistency, clarity, YAGNI) with a critical list for TODO/placeholder text and an approved/issues-found output format, so every spec gets the same dispatch via the general-purpose Task tool.

nodes.label: Plan Document Reviewer Prompt Template
nodes.rationale: Standardizes the plan-chunk reviewer's checks (completeness, spec alignment, task decomposition, checkbox task syntax, chunk size under 1000 lines) so each chunk is verified to match the spec and be implementation-ready before proceeding.

nodes.label: Browser Displays, Terminal Commands Architecture
nodes.rationale: Refactors visual brainstorming from a blocking TUI feedback model to a non-blocking model: the browser becomes an interactive display while the terminal stays the conversation channel, and the server writes user events to a per-screen .events file that Claude reads on its next turn, eliminating wait-for-feedback.sh and all TaskOutput blocking.

nodes.label: .events File Mechanism
nodes.rationale: The server appends each browser interaction (click/choice) as a JSON line to a per-screen .events file and clears it when a new screen is pushed; Claude reads it on the next turn and merges the structured interaction data with the user's terminal text, where the terminal message is the primary feedback.

nodes.label: helper.js Simplification
nodes.rationale: Narrows the client-side helper.js by removing sendToClaude, window.send, form/input handlers and the pageshow listener, keeping only click capture on [data-choice] elements plus indicator-bar updates and a minimal window.brainstorm API (send/choice).

nodes.label: frame-template.html Selection Indicator Bar
nodes.rationale: Replaces the feedback-footer HTML/CSS with a selection indicator bar and a <!-- CONTENT --> placeholder, and swaps wrapInFrame for comment-based content injection, so fragments get a header/theme/indicator while full documents are served as-is.

nodes.label: visual-companion.md Non-Blocking Loop Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Rewrites the brainstorming skill's loop to the non-blocking flow: write a fresh semantic-named HTML file, end the turn and tell the user to respond in the terminal, then on the next turn read $SCREEN_DIR/.events and merge it with the terminal text, iterating or advancing only after the current screen is validated.

nodes.label: server.js (zero-dependency replacement)
nodes.rationale: Core deliverable: single zero-dep server.js built only on Node built-ins (http, crypto, fs, path) replacing the vendored index.js + node_modules.

nodes.label: WebSocket Protocol Layer (RFC 6455)
nodes.rationale: Hand-written RFC 6455 text-frame codec (handshake, encode/decode, masking) so no `ws` dependency is needed.

nodes.label: computeAcceptKey
nodes.rationale: SHA-1 + WS_MAGIC base64 handshake response per RFC 6455; exported for unit testing.

nodes.label: encodeFrame
nodes.rationale: Server-side unmasked frame encoder with 3 length encodings (<126, 16-bit, 64-bit).

nodes.label: decodeFrame
nodes.rationale: Client-frame masked decoder returning {opcode, payload, bytesConsumed} or null when incomplete; throws on unmasked frames.

nodes.label: OPCODES constant
nodes.rationale: TEXT/CLOSE/PING/PONG opcode map shared by encode/decode and the connection handler.

nodes.label: HTTP Server + Request Handler
nodes.rationale: http.createServer handler serving the newest screen at /, static assets under /files/, and injecting helper.js.

nodes.label: fs.watch Screen-Dir Watching
nodes.rationale: Watches SCREEN_DIR for .html changes, debounces 100ms, logs screen-added/updated and broadcasts reload.

nodes.label: handleUpgrade (WebSocket connection)
nodes.rationale: Performs 101 handshake, manages the client socket set, and dispatches decoded frames to message/close/ping/pong.

nodes.label: broadcast
nodes.rationale: Encodes a TEXT frame and writes it to every connected client socket.

nodes.label: startServer
nodes.rationale: Creates the screen dir, starts the HTTP server + upgrade handler + fs.watch, and writes .server-info on listen.

nodes.label: start-server.sh swap (index.js -> server.js)
nodes.rationale: Decision to retarget lines 94/100 of start-server.sh at server.js so the launcher uses the zero-dep file.

nodes.rationale: Decision to git rm index.js, package.json, package-lock.json, and the entire node_modules tree, eliminating the dependency footprint.

nodes.rationale: Plan to make superpowers defer to native harness worktree systems when available, fall back to manual git worktrees when not, and fix three known finishing bugs (PRI-974)

nodes.label: Step 1a Native Worktree Tool Preference
nodes.rationale: Load-bearing assumption of the design: agents prefer native worktree/workspace-isolation tools (e.g. EnterWorktree) over git worktree add; native tools handle directory placement, branch creation, and cleanup automatically

nodes.label: Step 1b Git Worktree Fallback
nodes.rationale: Manual git worktree creation used only when no native tool is available, with directory priority (instructions > existing project-local dirs > default .worktrees/) and mandatory git check-ignore verification to prevent committing worktree contents

nodes.label: Step 0 Existing Isolation Detection (GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON)
nodes.rationale: Detect before creating anything: if GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON and not a submodule, already in a linked worktree, so skip creation and never create a nested worktree; includes opt-in consent prompt (#991) before creating a worktree in a normal checkout

nodes.label: Submodule Guard for Worktree Detection
nodes.rationale: GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON is also true inside git submodules, so git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree must be checked before concluding already in a worktree

nodes.label: Hooks Symlink After Manual Worktree Creation
nodes.rationale: Git worktrees do not inherit the parent repo's hooks directory; symlink .git/hooks from the main repo so pre-commit checks and linters do not silently stop

nodes.label: Provenance-Based Worktree Cleanup
nodes.rationale: Only clean up worktrees under .worktrees/ or worktrees/ (created by superpowers); harness-owned workspaces are left in place to avoid phantom state; merge first, verify, remove worktree from main repo root, then delete branch, with git worktree prune for self-healing

nodes.label: Visual Brainstorming Companion — Issue & Change Catalog
server.cjs — zero-dep HTTP + WebSocket server (RFC 6455 hand-rolled)
helper.js — injected page script (WebSocket client, click capture, window.brainstorm API)
frame-template.html — frame (header, theme CSS, status dot) around content fragments
start-server.sh — launch wrapper (session dir, host/url, owner-PID, backgrounding)
stop-server.sh — kills server by PID file, cleans /tmp sessions
visual-companion.md — operator guide the agent reads when it accepts the companion
SKILL.md — where the companion is offered and the per-question decision lives
A1 — per-session secret key on /, /files/*, and WS (chosen approach; supersedes Host allowlist)
nodes.rationale: A per-session secret key is the only mechanism that authenticates a client uniformly across loopback, SSH tunnel, and direct-remote, and also defeats DNS rebinding; a Host allowlist only defends the loopback browser confused-deputy and is theater for remote exposure, where a direct client just sends the expected Host.

nodes.label: A2 — Host allowlist dropped; browser WS Origin check retained after auth
nodes.rationale: Subsumed by A1: the secret key closes the WS-injection vector (#1014), the DNS-rebinding read vector (PR #1553), and the cross-origin WS vector (PR #1110) in one mechanism, and unlike an allowlist it actually protects the remote-bind case.

nodes.label: A3 — server crashes on null / non-object WS payload
nodes.rationale: JSON.parse can't produce undefined and primitives return undefined for .choice without throwing, so only null is the live hazard (null.choice throws); a minimal exact guard is preferred over a top-level try/catch or uncaughtException handler because those would mask other bugs.

nodes.label: A4 — frame-length bound in decodeFrame (already fixed; verify/close #1446)
nodes.rationale: MAX_FRAME_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 10MB is already enforced before any Buffer.alloc, so the action is to verify #1446 against current dev and close it rather than re-implementing.

nodes.label: B1 — macOS resource-fork dotfiles (._*.html) served as screen content
nodes.rationale: The newest-screen selector filters only on endsWith('.html'), so on macOS/ExFAT resource-fork files pass the filter and, being written alongside the real file, can sort newest — the browser gets binary metadata instead of the mockup.

nodes.label: B2 — stop-server.sh can kill a reused/stale PID
nodes.rationale: After a reboot or PID wraparound the state/server.pid file can point at an unrelated process, which would then be SIGKILLed; ownership must be verified (node running server.cjs) and the script should fail closed with stale_pid if it can't be proven.

nodes.label: B3 — WS client silent reconnect and stale 'Connected' status
nodes.rationale: A fixed 1s reconnect timer with no onerror handler and a hardcoded 'Connected' status means that when the laptop sleeps or the server restarts, the page shows 'Connected' over a dead socket and queues events with no feedback.

nodes.label: C1 — idle timeout too short / not configurable; WS keeps process alive
nodes.rationale: A single brainstorm question can sit longer than the hardcoded 30-minute idle timeout while the user thinks or steps away, so the server dies mid-session; also shutdown() never closes upgraded sockets, so an open browser connection can keep the Node process alive past shutdown.

nodes.label: C2 — server death is invisible to user/agent
nodes.rationale: The skill is only soft-guided to check state/server-stopped, a guidance the model skips, and the browser shows a generic 'can't be reached' — so the user diagnoses manually and the agent keeps referring to a dead URL.

nodes.label: D1 — permanent opt-out of the visual companion (issue #892, deferred)
D2 — free-text feedback from the browser (issue #957, deferred)
nodes.rationale: The client only captures clicks on [data-choice], so a user who wants to annotate a mockup must switch to the terminal, breaking the visual flow; server persistence must also be extended because it only writes events with a truthy choice.

nodes.label: D3 — auto-open the companion URL (done in PR #1720 via --open)
D4 — light/dark contrast helpers in the frame (PR #1683, deferred)

No-subagents contract (implementers and reviewers never dispatch subagents)
nodes.rationale: A worker-spawned reviewer duplicates the task review the controller dispatches anyway - a full extra review seat per task - and its verdict counts for nothing in the process; a worker-spawned reviewer is a defect to flag, not rigor.

nodes.label: Event-subscription waiting (wait_agent is a subscription, not a poll)
nodes.rationale: A long wait wakes the moment a child produces mailbox activity, with the same latency as a short one; short-timeout polling buys nothing and costs a tool call and a context rebill per poll, and roughly two-thirds of measured wait calls were short polls that timed out.

nodes.label: Bounded wait stretches with reconciliation
nodes.rationale: A 5-10 minute bounded stretch keeps nearly all of a long wait's efficiency while guaranteeing a stuck or lost child is noticed within minutes rather than at the end of the session; after each stretch post one status line, run list_agents, and chase any child that finished without reporting.

nodes.label: Three-path classification (spike / bounded / architectural)

nodes.label: Approval-gate invariant (ceremony scales, approval never does)
nodes.rationale: Every path ends with the human partner approving intent before implementation; a todo list or one-function utility may have a two-sentence chat design, but it must be presented and approved - 'simple' tasks are where unexamined assumptions cause the most wasted work, and what scales with simplicity is the artifact, never the approval.

nodes.label: Explicit model + reasoning_effort on every spawn with config backstop
nodes.rationale: Setting model alone is a trap because the child's effort silently resets to that model's default; a machine-level default_subagent_model/default_subagent_reasoning_effort backstop in ~/.codex/config.toml routes any slipped spawn to a deliberate tier instead of silently inheriting the session's most expensive model.

nodes.label: Append-only hypothesis log with pre-registration
nodes.rationale: Corrections are new dated entries, never edits, and every battery gets a pre-registration entry BEFORE it runs, so the log stays a non-revisable record of what was predicted versus what was measured.

nodes.label: Pre-registration rule (criterion logged before the battery runs)

nodes.label: Bump-Only Manifest Preflight

nodes.label: Fallback token isolation on port fallback
nodes.rationale: When the preferred port is occupied, fallback servers reusing a persisted .last-token could create two live same-project servers sharing one bearer key; on fallback the loaded token is discarded and a fresh unpersisted token generated, and an explicit BRAINSTORM_TOKEN env override fails closed because the occupied server may use the same explicit token.

nodes.label: Stop-server process ownership proof (instance id argv)
nodes.rationale: stop-server.sh could signal an unrelated node server.cjs when strong ownership proof is unavailable; a per-start --brainstorm-server-id=<id> argv token (stored in state/server-instance-id, owner-only) is matched as a full argv token (/proc/<pid>/cmdline preferred, wide ps fallback), and the stop fails closed (not_running/stale_pid outcomes) because it is intentionally better to leave a stale process running than kill an unrelated one.

nodes.label: Deterministic test hardening (macOS and Windows Git Bash)

nodes.rationale: The originally hypothesized RED failure (blind adoption of a stale foreign ledger) did not reproduce — 25/25 RED reps refused to skip work — so the SKILL.md change proceeded on structural grounds (serf cross-plan collisions, overwritten briefs, git contamination) with maintainer sign-off 2026-07-06, not on a demonstrated error rate. The GREEN round claims only regression safety (same-plan resume still resumes) and a measured cost comparison; the raw tool-call count did not drop (S1 GREEN mean 9.6 vs RED probe 9.0), and the load-bearing result is that no GREEN rep needed commit-content forensics — disambiguation is now structural via the plan-scoped workspace and identity line.

nodes.label: Scenario S1 — stale ledger from a different plan
nodes.rationale: Post-upgrade worst case: a legacy flat ledger at .superpowers/sdd/progress.md with plan A's five complete lines, PLUS plan A's own completed plan-scoped workspace, and no workspace for plan B. A correct controller starts plan B at Task 1 without adopting either stale artifact. GREEN 5/5 all resolved structurally (workspace resolution + identity line), none via commit-content forensics.

nodes.rationale: Regression control: plan B Tasks 1-2 genuinely implemented (real code satisfying each spec, committed, recorded in the ledger). Both RED (v3 flat) and GREEN (v3 scoped) arms passed 5/5 on the truthful v3 fixture; v1/v2 S2 controls had failed 5/5 for fixture-fabrication reasons (placeholder hashes, stub code), not skill failure.

T1: SDD worker-review prohibition
nodes.rationale: 9/9 depth-2 spawns across 4 corpora were implementer-issued reviewer subagents, all duplicates of the review the controller dispatches anyway; the dispatch contract never says review is not the worker's job, and 'self-review' in the implementer prompt gets reified into a reviewer subagent on harnesses where children can spawn (Codex). Fix: explicit 'you do not dispatch subagents' clause plus a Red Flags row, graded by score_e6.py/score_e5.py against baseline 9/9 worker-issued.

nodes.label: T2: Event-driven waiting
nodes.rationale: 60-78% of wait_agent calls time out in every corpus (dev 67.1%, spinout 60.2%); source recon shows V2 waits are event subscriptions, not polls - one long wait has the same wake latency as a 10s poll at ~1/90th the calls, and a completed child's FINAL_ANSWER is pushed into the parent's mailbox. Fix: never short-timeout poll; when idle issue ONE wait_agent with timeout_ms 900000+; criterion timeout rate < 25%.

nodes.label: T3: codex-tools.md corrections
nodes.rationale: Five claims in the current guidance are contradicted by the Codex source (all file:line-cited): close_agent does not exist in multi-agent V2 (V1-only; V2 LRU-evicts finished children), fix rounds can always resume the implementer via followup_task, role files attach to spawns via agent_type on isolated forks (0.145+), full-history forks accept model/reasoning_effort overrides (only agent_type refused), and the V2 spawn allowlist is v2 presets only (others hard-error). Fix: rewrite the multi-agent paragraph version-honest (V1 vs V2 labeled).

nodes.label: T4: Brainstorming three-path router (variant C)
nodes.rationale: The current HARD-GATE text pushes a bounded task to FULL ceremony 5/5, while Z-null (no guidance) and a three-path router both differentiate 5/5: absolute wording suppresses discrimination the model draws natively. The measured waste is the unconditional two-document artifact ritual (spec file -> plan file), not the approval gate. Variant C scales the ARTIFACT across spike/bounded/architectural paths while every path keeps human approval before implementation; guards: classification said out loud, heavier path when in doubt, one-way ratchet, Red Flags against classification-as-escape-hatch. Graded in three layers: adversarial micro, codex ceremony battery, and global regression battery on Claude Code/Gemini.

nodes.label: T5: Explicit model on child-issued spawns
nodes.rationale: Root spawns are 100% explicit-model at CLI 0.146 (dev 14/14), but the live gap is depth-2: 2/2 child-issued spawns omitted model. Source recon: model without reasoning_effort resets effort to the MODEL's default, not the parent's. Fix: every spawn sets model AND reasoning_effort, plus machine-level backstop via [agents].default_subagent_model / default_subagent_reasoning_effort in ~/.codex/config.toml. Pre-registered caveat: if T1 eliminates depth-2 spawns entirely, T5 grades as root-spawn regression (hold 100%) plus doc correctness and is recorded inconclusive-by-zero at depth-2.

nodes.label: Read-only preflight for version bump
nodes.rationale: Before a version bump writes any manifest, run one read-only preflight that validates the required tools and reads every present declared manifest through the dispatcher; this prevents a deterministic YAML failure from occurring after earlier JSON files have already been updated. It is the only reliability addition - it does not make the script transactional or redesign existing audit/error-status behavior; missing-file behavior stays unchanged and --help still works without jq or yq.

nodes.label: diagnosing-superpowers skill
nodes.rationale: Pure prose skill for v1 (no shipped scripts) that works with the user to pin down a wrong superpowers session, examines on-disk transcripts, and reports what happened with evidence; it reports, never diagnoses superpowers — that is the remote triager's job.

nodes.label: Problem intake step
nodes.rationale: Complaints usually arrive vague; intake asks one question at a time until the problem statement names the session, the turn range, and the observable, because the statement scopes everything downstream.

nodes.label: Skill timeline analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Skill triggering is a first-class analysis dimension: what fired when in response to what, and where a skill's trigger description matched the request but nothing fired or fired late.

nodes.label: Plan adherence analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Quality is judged as process evidence against the plan the session agreed to (design, plan, acceptance criteria, spec/plan files); plan drift after compaction and resume points is common, so those are marked.

nodes.label: Repeated work analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Detects the same file read or edited many times, the same command re-run, the same subagent task re-dispatched, and decisions re-derived after they were already made.

nodes.label: Stumbles analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Catches tool errors, failed commands, retries, reverted edits, backtracking, user corrections, permission denials, hook failures, API errors, crashes, and context overflow.

nodes.label: Quality evidence analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Checks whether 'done', 'verified', 'passing' claims are backed by verification output that precedes them, whether commits match claims, and whether review feedback was addressed; it is not a code review of the resulting diff.

nodes.label: Request conflicts analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Only human-typed prompts count as user instructions (hook output, system-reminder blocks, and tool results arrive with the user role), so contradictions are tracked across turns and against instruction files.

nodes.label: Cost and time analysis dimension
nodes.rationale: Accounts tokens (input, output, cache) and wall-clock per human turn, per subagent, and per tool; Claude Code carries per-message usage and Codex emits token_count events.

nodes.label: Context safety hard rule
nodes.rationale: Single transcript lines can hold 100k+ tokens (tool results, images, hook payloads), so never cat or grep a transcript for content: get counts and line numbers first, then extract small fields from specific lines.

nodes.label: Red Flags rationalization table
nodes.rationale: Rows are hypotheses from design; the shipped table is built from rationalizations observed in the RED phase baseline runs — rows that never show up are dropped, rows that do are reworded to match what agents actually said.

nodes.label: Fixed report section structure
nodes.rationale: Fixed section order so a remote triager can rely on it; the superpowers-involvement line (not indicated / possible / likely) is the only place the skill states a belief about superpowers, and it stops at involvement — no defect named, no change proposed.

nodes.label: Scrubbed bundle export step
nodes.rationale: A bundle is the user's own session data packaged for others, and being handed one unprompted feels intrusive, so the skill never builds a bundle unprompted; scrub and an independent scrub-audit repeat until the audit finds nothing, and a user gate approves before the archive is created.

nodes.label: GitHub issue filing step
nodes.rationale: Runs only when the report says superpowers involvement is possible or likely, or the user asks; nothing is posted anywhere without the user approving the exact text, and the template footer is the durable marker because GitHub drops labels from reporters without push access.

nodes.label: Similar sessions search step
nodes.rationale: Local machine only — the skill never reaches into other people's sessions or remote stores; discovery is metadata-first (mtime, size, then marker line numbers) to keep context safe.

nodes.label: Claude Code session store reference
nodes.rationale: Real field-level detail is given only for formats verified against files on disk (Claude Code 2.1.247): store layout, subagent transcripts, per-entry fields, attributionSkill/attributionPlugin, compact_boundary compaction, and hook payloads.

nodes.label: Codex session store reference
nodes.rationale: Verified against files on this machine (Codex CLI 0.147.0); Codex has no skill attribution field, so skill use is inferred from function_call reads of SKILL.md paths and multi-agent spawn records.

nodes.label: Other-harness discovery procedure
nodes.rationale: No invented formats: the running harness is expected to know its own session store, and the skill tells it to use that knowledge and say plainly what it could and could not read.

nodes.label: RED/GREEN/REFACTOR testing plan
nodes.rationale: Per writing-skills, no skill without a failing test first: baseline scenarios run on real transcripts with a known problem but without the skill, behavior and rationalizations are recorded verbatim, and the skill is written to the observed failures.

nodes.label: Plugin tests (tests/ suite)
nodes.rationale: Non-LLM code tests: bash/node/python integration tests for brainstorm-server JS, OpenCode plugin loading, codex-plugin sync, and analysis utilities.

nodes.label: Skill behavior evals (evals/ quorum harness)
nodes.rationale: Python harness driving real tmux sessions of Claude Code / Codex / Gemini CLI with an LLM actor and verifier judging skill compliance; quorum is the harness CLI.

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Polyglot Hooks for Claude Code
run-hook.cmd polyglot dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Single generic dispatcher that is a polyglot script: Windows parses the first block as batch, Unix treats it as a no-op heredoc and continues, so one file works on Windows/macOS/Linux.

nodes.label: Extensionless hook scripts
nodes.rationale: Hook scripts are extensionless (session-start, not session-start.sh) so Claude Code's Windows .sh auto-prepend does not inject 'bash' and break the dispatcher.

nodes.label: Brainstorming HARD-GATE
nodes.rationale: Before any implementation action, the human partner must approve the selected path's design artifact (spike probe, in-chat design, or written spec + plan); a reply approves only the stage presented.

nodes.label: Spike / Bounded / Architectural paths
nodes.rationale: The request is classified into one of three paths up front; when in doubt take the heavier one and hidden complexity only upgrades the path mid-task, never downgrades.

nodes.label: Visual Companion (browser mockup tool)
nodes.rationale: A just-in-time browser-based companion offered only when a question is clearer shown than told; per-question it decides browser vs terminal.

nodes.label: Analyst common prompt (role, inputs, return format)
nodes.rationale: Single shared role spec for all analyst subagents: read-only, evidence-first (finding + path:line + turns + confidence) so the dispatcher can verify and discard unsupported findings instead of letting the analyst editorialize.

nodes.label: Cost and time analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Accounts for where tokens and wall-clock went: token totals (incremental vs cumulative counter semantics), longest turns, idle gaps, largest tool results, compactions, and associated-session usage.

nodes.label: Plan adherence analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Recovers the agreed plan and maps each step to execution, flagging skipped/out-of-order/silently-changed/invented steps and drift right after structural events like compaction, since drift after context loss is a distinct failure mode.

nodes.label: Quality evidence analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Judges the process against its own claims (tests, verification behind 'done/verified' text, commit messages, review responses, acceptance criteria) rather than reviewing the produced code.

nodes.label: Repeated work analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Detects duplicated tool work by (tool, key) grouping with per-category thresholds, distinguishing benign re-reads-after-edit from re-reads-after-compaction or re-derived decisions, which indicate context loss.

nodes.label: Request conflicts analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Surfaces mutually unsatisfiable human instructions, conflicts with loaded instruction files, and skip/override instructions, reporting the conflict and resolution without judging the human.

nodes.label: Scrub auditor prompt
nodes.rationale: Independent privacy pass over an already-scrubbed bundle: find missed redactions and unresolved classifications, return CLEAN or MISSED lines, never the sensitive value itself, and never comment on scrub quality.

nodes.label: Scrubber prompt
nodes.rationale: Rewrites every file under BUNDLE to safe placeholders (stable value-to-placeholder mapping assigned in first-appearance order) so the bundle can leave the machine, with a scrub-log table that never leaks original values.

nodes.label: Similar-session matcher prompt
nodes.rationale: Decides whether a candidate transcript shows the same behavior as a diagnosed session by checking typed signature markers (skill-sequence, error-string, repeated-command/file, compaction-then, missed-trigger, free) and scoring yes/partial/no on path:line evidence.

nodes.label: Skill timeline analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Builds a per-human-turn record of skill/plugin/MCP/hook use and reports invoked skills, missed triggers (request matched a trigger description with no invocation), and late invocations, without judging whether the miss was wrong.

nodes.label: Stumbles analyst dimension
nodes.rationale: Finds every point where the session stopped going forward (errors, failed shell, retries, reverted edits, backtracking text, human corrections, denials, compactions) and reports recovery status for each, since stumble density is a core signal of how the session went wrong.

nodes.label: Context-safety rules for reading session transcripts
nodes.rationale: A single transcript record can exceed a megabyte or embed a whole history, so readers measure before reading, extract small fields from specific lines, narrow anything over 500 characters, and stay read-only to avoid overflowing the diagnosing session's own context.

nodes.label: GitHub issue search and filing workflow
nodes.rationale: Provides a degraded fallback chain (gh CLI -> unauthenticated API -> prefilled URL) for searching and filing issues in obra/superpowers, including label-landing caveats and the 8000-character URL limit, so issue reporting works in restricted environments.

nodes.label: Redaction policy and placeholder categories
nodes.rationale: Keeps exported bundles publishable without losing evidentiary value: redact emails, people, orgs, secrets, hosts, home paths, repos, and proprietary terms to stable placeholders while preserving session ids, tool/skill names, line numbers, and the safe command/result/source structure needed to verify findings.

nodes.label: Session discovery procedure
nodes.rationale: Resolves and confirms the named session from actual history (identity, not recency), establishes record meanings and counter semantics from observed records, and records everything in the case file so subsequent readers do not repeat discovery.

nodes.label: Diagnosis bundle README template
nodes.rationale: Defines the exportable bundle (report, case, environment.json, timeline, per-dimension findings, condensed transcripts, scrub-log) with three redaction levels, and requires producer-side evidence re-verification plus a separate privacy audit, because the bundle deliberately contains no diagnosis or fix - that is the reader's job.

TDD / RED-GREEN-REFACTOR Mapped to Skills
nodes.rationale: Skill creation follows the full RED-GREEN-REFACTOR cycle: run a baseline pressure scenario and watch the agent fail (RED), write the minimal skill that fixes those exact failures (GREEN), then close newly found loopholes (REFACTOR).

nodes.label: Testing Skills With Subagents (pressure scenarios)
nodes.rationale: You must watch an agent fail without the skill (baseline) before writing it, so you know the exact rationalizations to counter; subagent pressure scenarios (time, sunk cost, authority, exhaustion) are the RED phase of skill TDD.

nodes.label: Skill Discovery Optimization (SDO)
nodes.rationale: The description field must state only triggering conditions, never summarize the workflow, because testing revealed agents will follow a workflow-summarizing description as a shortcut and skip the full skill body.

nodes.label: The Iron Law — No Skill Without a Failing Test First
nodes.rationale: Writing skills IS Test-Driven Development applied to process documentation; if you did not watch an agent fail without the skill, you do not know the skill teaches the right thing. Applies to new skills and edits, no exceptions.

nodes.label: Match the Form to the Failure
nodes.rationale: The form that bulletproofs one baseline-failure type measurably backfires on another (e.g., prohibition lists backfire on wrong-shaped-output problems), so classify the baseline failure before choosing the guidance form.

nodes.label: Bulletproofing Skills Against Rationalization
nodes.rationale: Discipline-enforcing skills must resist rationalization: explicitly forbid specific workarounds, state a spirit-vs-letter principle, build a rationalization table from baseline tests, and add a red-flags list so agents can self-check under pressure.

nodes.label: Concise is key
nodes.rationale: The context window is a public good; once a SKILL.md is loaded, every token competes with conversation history and other context. Agents are already very smart, so only add context they don't already have.

nodes.label: Set appropriate degrees of freedom
nodes.rationale: Match the level of specificity to the task's fragility and variability: high freedom (text instructions) when many approaches are valid, low freedom (exact scripts) when operations are fragile and consistency is critical.

nodes.label: Test with all models you plan to use
nodes.rationale: Skills act as additions to models, so effectiveness depends on the underlying model; what works for Opus may need more detail for Haiku.

nodes.label: Naming conventions (gerund form)
nodes.rationale: Gerund-form names (verb + -ing) clearly describe the activity a Skill provides and make Skills easier to reference, organize, and search; vague names like Helper or Utils should be avoided.

nodes.label: Writing effective descriptions (third person)
nodes.rationale: The description field enables Skill discovery and is injected into the system prompt; agents use it to choose the right Skill from 100+ candidates, so it must state both what the Skill does and when to use it, in third person.

nodes.label: Progressive disclosure patterns
nodes.rationale: SKILL.md serves as an overview that points agents to detailed materials as needed; only metadata is pre-loaded, so keep the body under 500 lines and split content into separate files loaded only when relevant.

nodes.label: Keep references one level deep
nodes.rationale: Agents may partially read files that are referenced from other referenced files (e.g. head -100), resulting in incomplete information, so all reference files should link directly from SKILL.md.

nodes.label: Use workflows with checklists for complex tasks
nodes.rationale: Breaking complex operations into clear sequential steps with a copyable checklist prevents agents from skipping critical validation and helps both author and agent track progress.

nodes.label: Implement feedback loops (validate-fix-repeat)
nodes.rationale: The run-validator, fix-errors, repeat pattern catches errors early and greatly improves output quality; the validator can be a script or a reference document the agent checks against.

nodes.label: Build evaluations first
nodes.rationale: Creating evaluations before writing extensive documentation ensures the Skill solves real problems rather than documenting imagined ones; establish a baseline without the Skill, then iterate.

nodes.label: Develop Skills iteratively with the agent (Agent A / Agent B)
nodes.rationale: Work with one agent instance (Agent A) to design instructions and test with another (Agent B) on real tasks; iterating based on observed Agent B behavior rather than assumptions improves Skills.

nodes.label: Solve, don't punt (explicit error handling, no voodoo constants)
nodes.rationale: Scripts in Skills should handle error conditions explicitly instead of failing and letting the agent figure it out, and configuration values should be justified to avoid magic numbers (Ousterhout's law).

nodes.label: Provide utility scripts
nodes.rationale: Pre-made scripts are more reliable than generated code, save tokens and time, and ensure consistency; make clear whether the agent should execute a script or read it as reference.

nodes.label: Create verifiable intermediate outputs (plan-validate-execute)
nodes.rationale: Having the agent produce a structured plan file (e.g. changes.json) that a script validates before execution catches errors early, is machine-verifiable, and makes planning reversible without touching originals.

nodes.label: Avoid Windows-style paths (use forward slashes)
nodes.rationale: Unix-style paths with forward slashes work across all platforms, while backslash paths cause errors on Unix systems, even when the Skill is authored on Windows.

nodes.label: Provide a default, don't offer too many options
nodes.rationale: Presenting multiple approaches is confusing; give one default with an escape hatch for the alternative case instead of a menu of libraries or options.

nodes.label: Use fully qualified MCP tool names
nodes.rationale: MCP tools must be referenced as ServerName:tool_name because without the server prefix agents may fail to locate the tool when multiple MCP servers are available.

nodes.label: List and verify package dependencies
nodes.rationale: Skills run in code execution environments with platform-specific limitations (e.g. the API has no network access and no runtime package installation), so required packages must be listed and never assumed installed.

nodes.label: Runtime environment (filesystem-based access)
nodes.rationale: Metadata is pre-loaded at startup, files are read on-demand from the filesystem, and scripts execute without their contents consuming context tokens; this filesystem-based model is what enables progressive disclosure.

nodes.label: Checklist for effective Skills
nodes.rationale: A pre-sharing quality gate covering core quality (specific description, under 500 lines, consistent terminology, one-level-deep references), code and scripts (explicit error handling, validation steps), and testing (evaluations, all model tiers).

nodes.label: Authority (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Imperative, non-negotiable language ("YOU MUST", "No exceptions") eliminates decision fatigue and rationalization, so discipline-enforcing and safety-critical practices get followed even under pressure.

nodes.label: Commitment (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Requiring announcements and explicit choices binds the agent to prior statements, ensuring skills are actually followed and creating accountability in multi-step processes.

nodes.label: Scarcity (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Time-bound requirements and sequential dependencies ("Before proceeding", "Immediately after X") create urgency that prevents the 'I'll do it later' postponement of verification steps.

nodes.label: Social Proof (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Universal patterns ("Every time") and failure-mode framing ("X without Y = failure") establish norms and warn about common failures, reinforcing standards.

nodes.label: Unity (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Collaborative language and shared goals ("we're colleagues", "we both want quality") build in-group belonging, suited to collaborative and non-hierarchical workflows.

nodes.label: Reciprocity (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Use sparingly - it can feel manipulative and is rarely needed in skills because other principles are more effective.

nodes.label: Liking (Persuasion Principle)
nodes.rationale: Don't use for compliance: it conflicts with an honest feedback culture and creates sycophancy, so it is avoided whenever discipline is being enforced.

nodes.label: Parahuman Model of LLM Behavior
nodes.rationale: LLMs respond to the same persuasion principles as humans because they are trained on human text where authority language precedes compliance, commitment sequences are frequently modeled, and social-proof patterns establish norms.
